html:
Roman general and politician, Julius Caesar's right-hand man, who later ruled the eastern half of the Roman world with Cleopatra and lost it to Octavian.

He served under Caesar in the last years of the Gallic Wars, fled Rome to join him as the civil war began, and was his co-consul in 44 BCE. After the murder his funeral speech turned the crowd against the killers. Cicero attacked him in the Philippics, and Antony never forgave him.

In 43 BCE he joined Octavian and Lepidus in the Second Triumvirate. Together with Octavian he beat Brutus and Cassius at Philippi in 42 BCE, and then took the east. There he allied with Cleopatra of Ptolemaic Egypt and had three children with her, though he married Octavian's sister Octavia in 40 BCE. His invasion of the Parthian Empire in 36 BCE was a costly failure.

Octavian turned Rome against him as a man ruled by a foreign queen. At Actium in 31 BCE their fleet was beaten. A year later, with Octavian at the gates of Alexandria, Antony killed himself, and Cleopatra soon after. Octavian became Augustus.
